newsitem.title: UK: LME aluminium surges, profit taking trims others.
newsitem.headline: LME aluminium surges, profit taking trims others.

text.p: LME aluminium pushed higher to a bullish finish on Wednesday while copper and nickel eased off their peaks as players locked in profits.
Aluminium surged during the last few mintues of the afternoon kerb and ended at a fresh seven month high of $1,590, the strongest since May 31, 1996.
The technical outlook was positive after three month prices gapped higher in the morning, analyst William Adams of broker Rudolf Wolff said.
"The close above $1,580 is very positive," he said, adding that charts were showing a reverse head and shoulders pattern.
The long-term target was now around $1,800, with the first resistance level coming in at $1,609, Adams said.
Consumer buying is seen at least partially responsible for the recent run-up in prices, analysts said.
"But we need to see significant drawdowns in LME stocks before we see much more progress," Angus MacMillan of broker Billiton said.
Stocks have remained stubbornly high at just under one million tonnes and have been on the rise again after putting in a series of declines from mid-November to mid-December.
They rose on Tuesday by 1,525 tonnes to 957,375 tonnes.

Copper marched up to a high of $2,253 earlier in the day on nearby tightness and positive charts, but when prices failed to breach resistance they drifted back on profit taking to close the afternoon kerb at $2,240, up $19.
The market on Tuesday shrugged off an increase in LME stocks, when data showed the bulk was in Singapore and was unlikely to help allieviate shortages in Europe and the US.
The premium of cash over three months metal firmed again on Wednesday, ending the day at $135/$138, up $15 from Tuesday.
Resistance was pegged around $2,250, then the November 28 high of $2,313, with support seen from $2,215 to $2,225.
Nickel also came off its peak after blistering New Year gains that saw it add over $800 or 12 percent in a few days.
Profit-takers came in on Wednesday after prices stalled at a peak of $7,250, and prices ended the day at $7,115, up $35 on the day.
"After those kind of gains it needs a bit of a pause," Adams said. If the market can consolidate above $7,000, it should be able to gather enough steam to later push higher, he added.
Until now, most of the run-up has has seemed to been due to fund short covering, with other buying still to come, Adams said.
The others were mixed, holding to relatively narrow ranges.
Tin held within its sideways trading band over the past month, adding $20 to $5,800.
Chartist Harry Creates of broker AMT pegged important support at $5,745 and key resistance at $5,880.
Lead declined $9 to $695 and zinc lost $7 to $1,065.
Alloy finished firmer at $1,470/80 versus $1,445.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8065
